newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy seen running lower April deficit -- report.
newsitem.headline: Italy seen running lower April deficit -- report.

text.p: Italy is expected to run a public sector deficit in April of 12 to 13 trillion lire compared to a 25 trillion lire deficit in April 1996, an Italian newspaper reported on Sunday.

If the forecast for April is confirmed, Italy will have a cumulative deficit for the first four months of the year of 34 to 35 trillion, around half the 70.4 trillion lire deficit run up in the same period last year, Milan business daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported.

The newspaper said that if present trends continued the government's target of bringing the ratio of the public sector deficit to gross domestic product down to three percent in 1997 could be in sight.
"If things go on like this, the ratio of three percent between the deficit and domestic product will no longer be a mirage," Il Sole said.
The three percent deficit target is a key qualifying criterion for membership of European economic and monetary union (EMU), planned for launch in 1999.
The government last month introduced a supplementary budget of 15.5 trillion lire worth of deficit-cutting measures.
Treasury figures released at the weekend showed that tax revenues were expected to rise 7.5 percent to 544 trillion lire in 1997 from the previous year.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has announced a series of increases in utility charges in 1997, led by water, set to rise by 91.4 percent, postal charges, by up to 10 percent.
Motorway tolls and rail fares are set to rise by 3.20 percent and 2.16 percent, respectively.
